wikiGoal:
# Benchmark documentation brief

Create a source-grounded wiki for engineers who must understand, operate, debug, and safely change this repository.

- Explain the architecture, ownership boundaries, core data/control flows, persistence, external integrations, configuration, and failure handling.
- Include a practical quickstart and focused change guides for representative maintenance tasks.
- Treat source code and tests as authoritative. Cite concrete source evidence for every non-obvious technical claim.
- State uncertainty when the repository does not establish a fact. Do not invent runtime behavior, guarantees, or deployment details.
- Prefer a coherent, non-overlapping taxonomy over exhaustive file-by-file narration.

pages.title: Agent Host
pages.purpose: Document the utilityProcess Agent Host: session lifecycle, handlers, session index/watcher, model runtime, auth, skills/plugins, file access, worktrees, and title generation.
instructions: Cover crash/liveness behavior: uncaughtException exits, main supervises and restarts.
Cover session file persistence under ~/.pi/agent, the session index, watcher debounce, and file-access root policy.
Explain how the Host runs pi-coding-agent in-process and serves Api/Streams over MessagePort.

pages.title: Electron Main Process
pages.purpose: Document the Electron main process desktop shell: window lifecycle, tray, menus, deep link, protocol, single instance, updates, diagnostics, host supervision, and desktop IPC.
instructions: Cover Host supervision: spawn, ping heartbeat, crash restart budget, before-restart managed process cleanup.
Cover desktop IPC (installDesktopIpc), menu/tray/deep-link events, and the app:// protocol.
Cover the update manager lifecycle, platform gating, and install failure recovery.

pages.title: Architecture Overview
pages.purpose: Explain the Electron three-process architecture, ownership boundaries, main data/control flows, and security posture.
instructions: Explain where each capability is owned (main vs agent-host vs renderer) and how data flows between them without local TCP servers.
Focus on the process model: Electron main, utilityProcess Agent Host, sandboxed renderer, Main-owned WebContentsView, and managed project processes.

pages.title: Renderer and Preload Bridge
pages.purpose: Document the sandboxed React renderer and preload bridge: piBridge surface, MessagePort handoff, RPC client, host restart/crash recovery, theme, and i18n.
instructions: Explain renderer reconnection on host restart and the crash screen.
Explain that MessagePort must cross the contextBridge via window.postMessage transfer, and the early-event-replay buffering for menu/deep-link events.
Explain theme init and i18n dictionary structure at a high level.

pages.title: Typed MessagePort RPC and the Contract Layer
pages.purpose: Document the type-safe MessagePort RPC protocol, the Api/Streams contract, leases, error mapping, and how renderer, main, and Agent Host wire together.
instructions: Describe the five wire message kinds, subscription semantics with keys, call timeouts, leases, and error serialization.
Explain the two distinct transports: direct renderer-to-Host MessagePort and main-process host-rpc calls bridged through HostManager.

pages.title: Change Guide: Adding a Host RPC Method
pages.purpose: Focused maintenance guide for adding a new request/response API method end-to-end across the contract, Host handler, renderer client, and contract-coverage check.
instructions: Mention error mapping conventions (RpcError codes, ToolchainError mapping).
Walk through the concrete steps: type in Api, register handler, expose renderer helper, verify with check:contract, test with a focused .test.mjs.

pages.title: Change Guide: Managed Process Policy
pages.purpose: Focused maintenance guide for changing managed-process validation, limits, or backend behavior, including tests and platform gates.
instructions: Walk through changing MANAGED_PROCESS_LIMITS or BLOCKED_COMMANDS, how tests cover it, and how the capability gate affects packaged builds.

pages.title: Build, Packaging, and Verification
pages.purpose: Document the build pipeline, packaging matrix, CI workflows, verification/check scripts, and release artifacts.
instructions: Describe platform packaging targets and the Windows helper/SBOM build steps; do not invent release/deployment details the repo does not establish.
Explain the three tsup bundles (main CJS, agent-host/workers ESM, preload), the Vite renderer build, and where output lands.
List the verification gate scripts referenced by verify.mjs and what each checks.

pages.title: Persistence and Data Locations
pages.purpose: Cross-cutting reference for where state persists: Pi sessions/config under ~/.pi/agent, Electron userData for desktop settings, credentials, grants, reaper journal, and toolchain state.
instructions: Explain atomic-write patterns (models.json) and version-conflict handling.
Explain which persistence is intentionally not durable (e.g., runtime grants, ephemeral browser profiles).
Give concrete paths and JSON file names where the code establishes them; state uncertainty where a path is derived at runtime.

pages.title: Built-in Browser
pages.purpose: Document the Main-owned WebContentsView browser: profiles, settings, network policy, authorization model, CDP coordination, agent browser tools, and advanced mode.
instructions: Explain advanced mode gating (this-launch switch), CDP network capture, write request replay with confirmation, and the private-network best-effort caveat.
Explain permission levels, session grants, persistent grants, authorization dialogs, and that Coding permissions never imply browser permissions.
Explain that remote sites and localhost project pages load in Main-owned WebContentsView without app preload/Node access.
State uncertainty explicitly where the repo does not establish behavior.

pages.title: Managed Background Processes
pages.purpose: Document the managed-process system end-to-end: policy validation, agent tools, service, output buffers, log cursors, platform backends, crash reaper, and shutdown cleanup.
instructions: Cover command validation (blocked commands, LAN bind confirmation), cwd containment, output redaction, and limits.
Cover platform backends: POSIX process groups vs Windows Rust helper + Job Object, owner identity, and fail-closed behavior.
Cover the main-process reaper journal, before-restart cleanup, and shutdown deadline.
Explain the feature is off by default and is lifecycle control, not a sandbox; subprocesses inherit host filesystem/network/env privileges.

pages.title: Messaging Channels (WeChat, Telegram, Feishu/Lark)
pages.purpose: Document the IM channel subsystem: adapters, config/state persistence, pairing, bindings, session bridge, media handling, and policy.
instructions: Explain account secrets persisted via main-process credential vault, bindings, tool permission policy per Pi session, and redaction.
Explain outbound-only long polling (WeChat/Telegram) and outbound WebSocket (Feishu); no inbound webhooks or listening ports.
Explain per-channel rich rendering and media conversion (SILK to WAV).

pages.title: Toolchain Management
pages.purpose: Document toolchain discovery, catalog, managed installs, project resolution, and runtime environment that pi-coding-agent sessions consume.
instructions: Explain bundled rg/fd offline search and managed components install into an app-private directory without touching system PATH.
Explain the capability model (ToolCapabilityId), providers (system/custom/bundled/managed), health states, and preferences.
Explain the snapshot/ack flow: main publishes ToolchainSnapshot, Host acknowledges by revision, and the packaged-startup validation gates on it.

pages.title: Quickstart
pages.purpose: Get engineers up and running: environment requirements, dev loop, build, test, verify, packaging commands, and task routing across the wiki.
instructions: Include a task-routing map linking common maintenance tasks to the relevant wiki pages.
Include only commands and facts that are verifiable from package.json scripts and the scripts/ directory.
